idea: Italian speciality food export brokerage to UK and Asia
buyer: UK and Asian importers, delis, restaurant groups
pain: Small Italian producers cannot reach export markets
v1: Broker one producer into two UK buyers
verdict: Real access but a low-margin trading business using almost none of her expensive skills.

why.distribution: Producer side is warm via her husband; buyer side is cold and fragmented.
why.demand: Food import brokerage is a real functioning market with established margins.
why.fmf: Almost none of her expertise applies. This is food trading, not analysis.
why.revenue_structure: Commission per order, repeating if relationships hold.
why.defensibility: Food brokers are numerous and margins are competed away.
why.tailwind: Flat, with post-Brexit import friction working against it.
why.ceiling: 10% on £600k of orders = £60k, and £600k of brokered food orders is a serious operation.

ceiling_arithmetic: 10% commission on £600k of orders = £60k. Reaching that order volume requires a real trading operation with logistics and credit risk. Structurally capped well below target.
carries: Genuine producer access through a trusted family connection.
kills: It wastes her advantage entirely and the margin structure cannot reach the target.
test: Ask two UK importers whether they want new Italian suppliers.
